messages:
jamie: thanks for staying after the town hall — quick follow-up on the budget slide, a few people asked for clarification so posting answers here.

nina: can you confirm current runway in months at our FY targets? seemed like numbers changed between slides.

elaine: short answer: ~18 months under current plan. we modeled a conservative case with hiring pauses in Q3 if growth slows.

sam: to add, the 18mo uses the commit-level plan (no Dedicated expansion). if we win a couple of large deals runway improves.

matt: breakdown if useful: burn today ~ $5.4M/mo; revenue growth assumptions baked in reduce net burn to ~$3.2M/mo by end of year. happy to share the model.

jamie: @matt can you drop the model link? and can you highlight which hires are considered "must-hire" vs "nice-to-have"?

matt: posted the sheet here: https://short.link/redwood-fin-model (view only). must-hires are infra ops (2 SWE-SRE), 1 security engineer, 2 sales AE. all others are backfilled or deferred.

olivia: what about spend controls? procurement team asked for clearer thresholds for purchases >$10k.

devon: yep — quick note: new approval path starting next week: anything >= $10k needs Finance + Cost Owner approval; >= $50k requires Exec sponsor. We've set up a Slack workflow for pre-approvals.

jamie: can you paste the workflow or example PO message? makes onboarding easier.

devon: sure, snippet below:
```
PO Request: {vendor, amount, cost_center, justification, term}
Approvals: cost-owner -> finance -> exec (if >=50k)
Expected SLA: 3 business days for standard vendors, 7 for new vendor onboarding
```

nina: new vendor onboarding SLA is worrying. we have a client integration that needs a vendor fast. any way to expedite?

devon: yes — tag me + @finance-bot and mark "expedite" in the form; will try to accelerate to 48-72 hours. new vendors only if legal + security sign-off.

elaine: reminder: we tightened discretionary spend last quarter. marketing promo budgets are scoped to campaigns approved by growth lead. please route all ad buys through procurement.

sam: transparency ask — can we get a monthly dashboard with top 10 spend categories and runway sensitivity? product and eng leaders find that helpful.

matt: will add a monthly snapshot in the finance channel and the Console (internal) — includes top vendors, committed reserved spend (Dedicated), and forecasted burn.

jamie: a couple Qs from folks: 1) any change to Dedicated reserved capacity purchases? 2) procurement card limits?

elaine: 1) Dedicated capacity line is still approved but new large commits require business case showing ROI within 9-12 months. 2) cards: default limit remains $5k; team leads can request temporary increases via procurement form.

olivia: can we get a checklist for business case expectations for Dedicated? engineers need to build the numbers into proposals.

matt: yes — I'll share a one-pager: expected throughput uplift, cost/unit comparison (on-prem vs Redwood Dedicated), contract term break-even.

nina: will the one-pager include quantization/ops savings assumptions? those matter a lot for cost/unit.

matt: yes — ops savings and projected token cost reductions by batching/kv-caching included.

jamie: thanks all. final ask — can leadership post a short FAQ in #all-hands summarizing the approvals and runway bullets for folks who missed the end?

elaine: will do a pinned post and a short Loom with the new procurement flow.

finance-bot: New procurement workflow live at 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z — use /po-request to start. :robot_face:

jamie: awesome, appreciate the quick follow-up. closing thread. :slightly_smiling_face:
